title: Special Systems: No Solution and Infinitely Many Solutions
description: Recognize parallel and overlapping lines, then use sliders, slope-intercept form, and proportions to find constants that create no solution or infinitely many solutions.

blocks.html:
Give it a try

Spend about a minute on this question. Keep your first idea, even if you are unsure. You can continue without submitting an answer.

shared_prompt.title: Opening question
shared_prompt.html: If \((k+1)x+my=8\) and \(9x+12y=24\) have infinitely many solutions, what is \(k+m\)?

blocks.html:
A solution count tells you what to match

The opening question hides constants but tells you the equations have infinitely many solutions. That tells us how their graphs must relate.

We’ll first compare two simple graph pictures, then use their slopes and intercepts to find exact constants.

Look for a shared point

Inspect the two lines. Do their paths meet or stay apart?

choices: The lines intersect exactly once at the point \((0,1)\).
The lines overlap each other at every point shown.
The lines stay the same distance apart and never intersect.
The lines intersect twice outside the visible window.
content.hint: Compare the lines' directions and the space between them as you pan.
content.explanation: The lines are parallel: they have the same direction but different positions, so they never intersect.

blocks.html:
Parallel lines have no shared solution

Parallel lines have the same slope and different y-intercepts. They never share a point, so the system has no solution. Here the slopes are both 2, while the intercepts are 1 and -3.

content.prompt: Which pair of equations represents a system with no solution?
content.hint: Look for equal slopes and unequal y-intercepts.
content.explanation: Both lines have slope \(-4\), but their y-intercepts are \(1\) and \(6\), so they are parallel and distinct.

blocks.html:
Show and hide the second line

Click the colored circle beside the second equation to toggle its graph. Does the visible path change?

calculator.title: Hide and show the overlapping line

figure.alt: The colored circle at the left of a Desmos expression row, which hides and shows that graph
figure.caption: Click the colored circle to hide or show a graph.

content.prompt: Why does this system have infinitely many solutions?
choices: The two lines are parallel to each other and therefore cannot touch.
The two lines share a y-intercept while keeping different slopes.
Each line contains infinitely many points, even though the lines are different.
Both equations create the same line, so every point on that line satisfies both equations.
content.hint: Hide either graph. Does the set of visible points change?
content.explanation: The second equation is twice the first equation, so both equations describe the same line and share every point.

blocks.html:
The same line shares every point

The equations \(2x+y=6\) and \(4x+2y=12\) both become \(y=-2x+6\). Their slope and intercept match, so every point on that line solves both: infinitely many solutions.

Same Slope, Then Intercept

  1. Rewrite each line as \(y=mx+b\), if needed.
  2. Match slopes for either special case.
  3. For no solution, keep intercepts different. For infinitely many, match them too.

A slider can help you see the target, but use the coefficients to establish an exact value.

shared_prompt.title: System with an adjustable slope
shared_prompt.html: Suppose the system is \(y=ax+1\) and \(y=2x-3\), and the question asks for the value of \(a\) that makes the system have no solution.

blocks.html:
See a slope change

Move A, which stands for a, toward a value that makes the lines parallel. Then compare the exact slopes to decide which value works.

calculator.title: Move A until the lines are parallel

content.prompt: Which value of \(a\) makes this system have no solution?
content.hint: Move the slider until both lines have the same direction. Read the value of A.
content.explanation: At \(a=2\), both lines have slope \(2\), while their y-intercepts remain \(1\) and \(-3\). They are distinct parallel lines.

blocks.html:
Confirm the slope exactly

In \(y=ax+1\), a is the slope. The other slope is 2, so a must equal 2. The intercepts are different, giving no solution.

shared_prompt.title: System with an adjustable intercept
shared_prompt.html: Now consider \(y=3x+b\) and \(2y=6x+8\). The question asks for the value of \(b\) that makes the system have infinitely many solutions.

blocks.html:
See an intercept change

Move B, which stands for b, until the lines overlap. Then compare their intercepts to determine the exact value.

calculator.title: Move B until the lines overlap

content.prompt: Which value of \(b\) makes this system have infinitely many solutions?
content.hint: Move B until hiding either graph leaves the same visible line.
content.explanation: Dividing the second equation by \(2\) gives \(y=3x+4\), so \(b=4\) makes the two equations identical.

blocks.html:
Expose the slopes and intercepts

\(ax+2y=10\) becomes \(y=-(a/2)x+5\). \(6x+3y=c\) becomes \(y=-2x+c/3\).

Now you can compare the slopes \(-a/2,-2\) and the intercepts \(5,c/3\).

Make the slopes match, with different intercepts

Set \(-a/2=-2\), giving a=4. For no solution, require \(c/3\ne5\), so \(c\ne15\). These conditions make distinct parallel lines.

content.prompt: Which condition makes the system have no solution?
content.solution:
Solve each equation for \(y\): \(ax+2y=10\) becomes \(y=-\frac{a}{2}x+5\), and \(6x+3y=c\) becomes \(y=-2x+\frac{c}{3}\).
No solution means parallel lines: same slope, different y-intercepts.
Match the slopes: \(-\frac{a}{2}=-2\), so \(a=4\).
Keep the y-intercepts different: \(\frac{c}{3}\ne5\), so \(c\ne15\). If \(c=15\) as well, the lines overlap and the system has infinitely many solutions instead.
So the answer is choice A, \(a=4\) and \(c\ne15\).
content.hint: No solution requires equal slopes but unequal y-intercepts.
content.explanation: \(a=4\) matches the slopes, and \(c\ne15\) keeps the intercepts different.

blocks.html:
Match both for the same line

The slope condition still gives a=4. Now match intercepts too: c/3=5 gives c=15. Both equations then describe the same line.

content.prompt: Which values make these equations represent the same line?
content.hint: Match both the slopes and the y-intercepts from the rewritten equations.
content.explanation: \(a=4\) makes both slopes \(-2\), and \(c=15\) makes both y-intercepts \(5\).

blocks.html:
Standard form can reveal a multiplier

For the same line, multiplying one whole equation by a nonzero number produces the other. The x-term, y-term, and constant all use that same multiplier.

This gives the same matching conditions without solving for y.

Use the common multiplier

Compare \(4x+6y=10\) with \(10x+ny=25\). The x-coefficient and constant both multiply by 2.5. For the same line, n must be 6(2.5)=15.

figure.alt: Coordinate graph of 4x+6y=10 and 10x+15y=25. A solid blue line and dashed orange line lie on the same path. Both have slope negative 2/3 and y-intercept 5/3, so every point on the line satisfies both equations.
figure.caption: At n = 15, the two equations describe the same line. The dashed path lies on the solid path.

blocks.html:
A different constant keeps the lines apart

For \(4x+6y=10\) and \(10x+15y=30\), both variable coefficients multiply by 2.5. But 10(2.5)=25, not 30. The slopes match while the intercepts differ: no solution.

figure.alt: Coordinate graph of 4x+6y=10 and 10x+15y=30. The solid blue line and dashed orange line are parallel. Both have slope negative 2/3, with y-intercepts 5/3 and 2 respectively, so the lines have no shared point.
figure.caption: The variable coefficients scale together, but the constants do not. The lines have the same slope and different intercepts.

blocks.html:
A requested ratio may be enough

If \(Ax+By=14\) and \(12x+18y=42\) represent the same line, \(A/B=12/18=2/3\). You can match the coefficient ratio without finding each coefficient first.

Return to the two constants

Try the opening question again. Use the condition on the solutions to decide what must match.

content.prompt: Return to the opening question. What answer do you get now?
content.hint: For the same line, one equation is a multiple of the other. Use the constants 8 and 24 to find that multiplier, then match both variable coefficients.
content.explanation: Multiplying the first equation by \(3\) gives the second: \(3(k+1)=9\), so \(k=2\), and \(3m=12\), so \(m=4\). Therefore, \(k+m=6\).
content.solution: Multiplying the first equation by \(3\) gives the second: \(3(k+1)=9\), so \(k=2\), and \(3m=12\), so \(m=4\). Therefore, \(k+m=6\).

content.prompt: How do the slope and intercept distinguish no solution from infinitely many solutions?
choices: No solution: equal slopes and equal intercepts; infinitely many: equal slopes and different intercepts.
No solution: different slopes; infinitely many: equal intercepts alone.
No solution: different slopes and different intercepts; infinitely many: equal slopes alone.
No solution: equal slopes and different intercepts; infinitely many: equal slopes and equal intercepts.
content.explanation: Equal slopes give parallel directions. Different intercepts keep the lines apart; equal intercepts make them the same line.

blocks.html:
Try it on your own

Choose the approach for each question. Try these now or save them for homework.

content.prompt: What kind of system is \(6x+9y=12\) and \(10x+15y=25\)?
choices: No solution: matching variable-coefficient ratios, different constant ratio.
Infinitely many: matching variable-coefficient ratios, regardless of the constant ratio.
One solution: matching variable-coefficient ratios and different constant ratio.
Two solutions: matching variable-coefficient ratios and different constant ratio.
content.explanation: The x- and y-coefficients scale by \(\frac{5}{3}\), but \(12\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)=20\), not \(25\). The lines are parallel and distinct.

content.prompt: The equations \(px+qy=20\) and \(15x+25y=50\) represent the same line. What is \(\frac{p}{q}\)?
content.explanation: \(\frac{p}{q}=\frac{15}{25}=\frac{3}{5}\). The individual values of p and q are unnecessary.

content.prompt: In the system of equations \(6x-9y=12\) and \(8x+ky=16\), \(k\) is a constant. If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of \(k\)?
content.explanation: \(\frac{8}{6}=\frac{16}{12}=\frac{4}{3}\), so the second equation is the first scaled by \(\frac{4}{3}\) and \(k=-9\cdot\frac{4}{3}=-12\). Copying \(-9\) skips the scaling, and \(-\frac{27}{4}\) inverts the factor.

content.html:
Same Slope, Then Intercept

Use exact coefficients to distinguish parallel lines from the same line.
